A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MidSteer work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. v1 Appendices I/J correspond to v2 K/L, allowing retained material to be distinguished from additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original concept-switching and erasure experiments on Llama, Qwen, SDXL and SANA, plus covariance-sample ablations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds safety-related switching experiments and GPT-4o-mini judge evaluations in Section 5 and Appendices I/J.

M1.justification: The LEACE-Switch and MidSteer transformations, steering-strength equations, covariance-estimation algorithm and weight-folding procedure remain unchanged. The safety experiments apply the existing method; added algorithm comments and rank discussion do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: v2 retains concrete object/character switching and erasure, and adds toxicity-to-helpfulness switching on Llama-2-7B-chat and Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, including RealToxicityPrompts. It also adds violence-to-peace switching on SDXL and SANA, with behavioral and emotional concepts used to assess preservation (Section 5; Appendix I).

E2.justification: The comparisons retain vanilla steering/CASteer and LEACE-Switch, with unsteered controls where reported; erasure comparisons also retain their comparator set. The new experiments extend these comparisons. Detoxify, ArmoRM and GPT-4o-mini are evaluators, not additional competing steering methods.

E3.justification: New safety protocols filter RealToxicityPrompts at prompt toxicity ≥0.5 and introduce Detoxify toxicity, ArmoRM helpfulness and MMLU BERT-F1 measurements. Appendix J adds GPT-4o-mini scoring across β=1–5 using the existing 0–10 prompt, without recomputing BERT-Precision. The retained concrete experiments keep their stated covariance sample sizes and evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: New Appendix J systematically tests sensitivity to judge choice on Llama-2-7B-chat across three concept pairs and five steering strengths, reporting source, target and unrelated-concept scores. v1 has no corresponding second-judge analysis. The covariance-sample ablation and earlier qualitative examples are retained, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The original ten randomized generations per template prompt remain documented, and the safety experiments use a similar seed-based practice. Neither version reports confidence intervals, variance estimates or significance tests. No increase in repetitions or new uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: The matched concrete-switching and erasure tables retain their numerical results. v2 Tables 2–9 add safety and alternative-judge outcomes: for example, Llama-2 toxicity is reported as 0.371 unsteered versus 0.281 for MidSteer at β=5, with helpfulness remaining 0.117. These are newly reported evaluations, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The optimization problems, closed-form solutions, corollaries and Appendix D proofs are mathematically unchanged. Section 3.2 re-explains guardedness, while Section 4.3 discusses the existing full-rank assumption; neither introduces a new theorem, formal relaxation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: connect steering to LEACE, derive LEACE-Switch, introduce directed minimal-disturbance MidSteer, and demonstrate effectiveness across language and vision. The additional experiments support these existing contributions without substantively redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds localized explanations of the nonzero source-covariance requirement, the stability rationale for 50,000 covariance prompts, and deployment side effects. It also interprets the new studies as supporting safety applicability and judge robustness. Some interpretations overreach: Table 2 does not give MidSteer the highest peace score, and Tables 7/11 contradict universal agreement of comparator rankings.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link, approximately one minute per 1,000 prompts on an H100 for cross-covariance estimation, covariance-reuse details, and judge API settings. However, it drops v1's Alpaca/RELAION covariance-data sourcing, caption-filtering instructions and GPT-o4-mini prompt-generation attribution; the referenced Appendix E does not restore these details.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Detoxify and ArmoRM and removes the Alpaca and LAION references accompanying deleted data-source descriptions. Its positioning relative to steering, affine erasure and distributional alignment remains essentially unchanged. The CASteer title/year update refers to the retained method, not a new comparator.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the guardedness explanation, separates concrete and safety experiments, inserts two appendix sections, expands the Impact Statement and adds acknowledgments. Author-affiliation and publication-header details also change. These are localized revisions within the retained overall argument and section sequence.

P2.justification: Eight new tables substantially expand the safety and judge-validation displays. Figure 2 corrects misplaced and duplicated panels using previously reported results, aligning plots with their Llama/SDXL captions. Appendix H's existing plot receives a figure number and caption; the other appendix plots and tables are largely retained, reflowed or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 improves Figure 2 and adds relevant safety evaluations, judge checks and practical explanations. However, new SDXL Tables 2 and 4 report unreconciled violence reductions of 99.6 to 6.0 versus 61.1 to 52.8. Section 5.2 also claims the strongest peace score despite Table 2 reporting 94.0 for MidSteer versus 96.5 for vanilla steering. Overstated judge agreement and lost covariance-data details further complicate the gains. These benefits and new reliability/reproducibility problems prevent a confident net quality judgment.
